title: Using [] operator or get() to access preloaded resources stored in array/dict from custom resource script(has at least two tres instances) causes parsing errors
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5.1stable, 4.4.1stable, 4.4stable, not test other versions

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7628) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12490F (12 threads) - 31.81 GiB memory

### Issue description

After careful review, I'm not sure if this issue is related to #105021. While the error messages appear somewhat similar, they seem to be distinct problems, so I've opened this as a separate issue.

#### Description
I have a custom resource script template that uses arrays or dictionaries to store preloaded it's resource instances(ensure at least two tres instances, otherwise no error). When I try to access these resources elsewhere using the [] operator or get() method, I encounter parse errors. However, if I expose a static method or public method in the custom resource script tempalte to retrieve the preloaded resources from its own arrays/dictionaries, it works fine. The error always occurs at the second defined preloaded resource statement from top to bottom.

It seems like a circular references problem? I'm not quite sure why it also happened in constants.

#### Demo:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40b695c0-139d-4c1b-a957-41b8743e19c9


### Steps to reproduce

Check the MRP, then try the two different ways to access preloaded resources in arrays/dictionaries.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[preload_2025-10-29_22-14-41.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23211965/preload_2025-10-29_22-14-41.zip)
